new_scholarship.name: Global Futures Scholarship
new_scholarship.duration: Payable for up to 3 years; the standard UK bachelor's degree runs 3 years full-time, or 4 years where the programme includes a Year in Industry
new_scholarship.deadline: Scholarship applications must be made on the dedicated online form by 4 March 2027 (North America round: Canada and the USA) or by Friday, 23 April 2027 (South East Asia round: Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam). The University states: "We cannot accept late applications under any circumstances."
new_scholarship.application_period: The academic application runs through UCAS with a 2027 Equal Consideration Deadline of 13 January 2027. The University emails the dedicated scholarship application form to relevant applicants and offer-holders from December 2026 onwards, and the form is open until each region's closing date.
new_scholarship.application_method: Separate application, not automatic on admission. Apply for the degree through UCAS (The University of Manchester's institution code is 3737, and UCAS is the only route to undergraduate admission); the University then emails a dedicated online scholarship application form to relevant applicants and offer-holders, which must be completed in full and submitted by the regional closing date. Students who applied before the UCAS Equal Consideration Deadline of 13 January 2027 may apply before holding an offer; students who applied after it must hold an offer before applying.
new_scholarship.description: The Global Futures Scholarship is The University of Manchester's international merit scholarship for students starting in September 2027, comprising more than 350 awards across undergraduate and master's study with a total value of more than GBP 6 million. For undergraduates the award is a partial tuition-fee discount of GBP 12,000 per year for up to three years, applied as a discount on published overseas tuition fees and conditional on an overall average of at least 60% in exams each year. Eligibility is determined by domicile rather than nationality and is restricted to applicants domiciled in the countries named for each regional round. Applicants must submit a dedicated online scholarship application form by the regional closing date, and the award cannot be combined with any other University of Manchester award.
new_scholarship.best_fit: High-achieving, self-funded school leavers domiciled in Canada, the USA, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Vietnam, applying for direct first-year entry to a full-time on-campus Manchester bachelor's degree for September 2027, who can meet the regional minimum grades (for example A Level AAA, IB 36 points with 666 at Higher Level, or three AP exams at 5,5,5) and want a substantial recurring tuition-fee discount rather than fully funded study.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Eligibility is based on domicile, not nationality: applicants must be permanently domiciled in a country named for their regional round (the North America undergraduate round covers Canada and the USA; the South East Asia round covers Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam) and must ordinarily and predominantly have resided in that country for the past three years, with residence there solely for full-time education not establishing domicile. Applicants must be international fee-paying and self-funded, meaning not sponsored by an external government agency or commercial funder; federal, provincial and private student loan recipients are eligible. They must be applying for direct first-year (Year 1) entry to a full-time, on-campus course in Manchester for September 2027, must not have previously studied at a higher education institution in the UK, and only one scholarship application may be submitted even where multiple courses are applied for. Medicine (MBChB), Dentistry (BDS), Architecture and courses with an integrated foundation year are excluded, as are blended and distance-learning programmes; students who applied unsuccessfully for MBChB or Dentistry and were then offered a different course remain eligible.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: No scholarship-specific test score is published; English is a condition of the academic course, set per programme. The University's policy page states that requirements vary by course and summarises typical scores for entry to Manchester as IELTS 5.5 up to 7.5 and above, TOEFL iBT 72 up to 109-120, Pearson PTE Academic 59-63 up to 79+, LanguageCert Academic 60 up to 81+ and Trinity ISE II up to ISE IV, with language tests valid for two years from the test date. The award terms require English offer conditions to be met by 15 July 2027 (AP, Dual Enrolment or IB), 13 August 2027 (A Level) or 15 August 2027 (South East Asia round). Nationals of UKVI majority English-speaking countries including the USA, and nationals of Canada for Student Route visa purposes, may be exempt from submitting further evidence.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Selection is competitive and primarily on academic merit: awardees are assessed on the UCAS application, predicted or achieved grades, results of previous tests and the strength of the personal statement and responses in the online application form. The University publishes no numerical weighting, and states it will also consider the overall composition of the scholarship cohort and may give greater credit to applicants for courses where students from their region are underrepresented, endeavouring for a balance by gender, domicile and qualification type. There is no interview and no portfolio. Notifications are issued by 5 April 2027 for the North America round and 1 June 2027 for the South East Asia round. Only the first scholarship application is considered where a student submits more than one, incomplete applications are not considered, and the decision of the selection panel is final with appeals not permitted.
new_scholarship.notes: TARGET NAME CORRECTION, stated plainly. The research brief named the award the 'Global Excellence Scholarship' with a value of GBP 6,000 per year and described it as not country-specific. None of that is confirmed on the official site: a request to /study/international/finance-and-scholarships/funding/global-excellence-scholarship/ returns HTTP 404 and the Wayback Machine holds no snapshot of that URL. The University's undergraduate international merit scholarship for 2027 entry is the Global Futures Scholarship, so that is what this record covers; it is a naming substitution, not a substitution of awarding body or of scholarship, and it is recorded in verification.unverified_or_removed_claims and research_notes. The verified undergraduate value for the North America and South East Asia rounds is GBP 12,000 per year for up to three years (GBP 36,000 in total, as the University itself states), not GBP 6,000; the earlier Faculty of Science and Engineering International Excellence Awards page (21 awards of GBP 5,000 per year for up to four years) refers to students starting in 2025 and is NOT part of the 2027-entry undergraduate funding list, so it was not used as a source of values or deadlines. Values, accepted qualifications, minimum grades, deadlines and notification dates vary by regional round: only the North America and South East Asia rounds were verified individually, and other regions' figures are flagged in institution_check_required rather than generalised. The recorded headline deadline is 4 March 2027, the earliest verified undergraduate closing date, chosen deliberately so that no applicant is misled into believing they have longer than their own round allows; the full set of published regional dates is in programme_detail_official.deadline_note. The logo key for manchester.ac.uk already exists in backend/config/official_logo_overrides.json pointing at this same URL, so logo_override repeats an existing entry and will be deduped at merge. All funding figures are per the University's published terms and conditions PDFs and country scholarship pages; no figure in this record was computed by the researcher.

programme_detail_official.deadline_note: There is no single scheme-wide deadline, so deadline_central records the earliest verified undergraduate closing date (4 March 2027, North America round) rather than a universal one. Verified 2027-entry undergraduate deadlines: North America round 4 March 2027; South East Asia round Friday 23 April 2027 (described as the final date to take up the award). Verified master's deadlines under the same programme name, which are outside this undergraduate record: 11 March 2027 (North America) and Friday 14 May 2027 (South East Asia). No closing time and no timezone are published for the online form, so deadline_central_timezone is null rather than guessed; applicants should treat the date as a calendar date and submit well before it. Downstream dates for the North America round are: offers of a study place required after the UCAS Equal Consideration Deadline of 13 January 2027; notification of the scholarship decision by 5 April 2027; Manchester to be the Firm UCAS choice by 5 May 2027; offer conditions, including English for AP, Dual Enrolment and IB applicants, met by 15 July 2027 and for A Level applicants by 13 August 2027. For the South East Asia round: notification by 1 June 2027, Firm UCAS choice by 7 June 2027, and all offer conditions including English met by 15 August 2027.
programme_detail_official.status_note: Open for 2027 entry. The scheme page published more than 350 awards for students starting in September 2027, scholarship forms are emailed from December 2026, and both verified undergraduate closing dates fall in 2027, so the cycle is live as of 2026-10-03. The next cycle is expected to run on the same annual pattern for 2028 entry, with pages and terms and conditions republished during 2027; the University does not state pre-announced 2028 dates.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Up to three years. For a standard three-year bachelor's degree the award is payable in Years 1-3; where a student registers for a course with a Year in Industry the award is applied to Years One, Two and Four, with continuation into Year Four dependent on performance in Year Two.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: Covers part of the published overseas (international) tuition fees only: GBP 12,000 per year for up to three years, applied as a discount on those tuition fees with no payment made to the awardee. It does not cover living costs, accommodation, travel, insurance, visa costs or the immigration health surcharge, and no stipend or cash amount is attached. Continuation is conditional on achieving overall marks of at least 60% in exams each year, so the discount is retained only while that condition is met. Because the award is tuition-only, leaves the remainder of tuition payable and covers none of the cost of living, fully_funded is false.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Part-funded: GBP 12,000 per year for up to three years (up to GBP 36,000 in total) as a discount on published overseas tuition fees, conditional on a 60% average in exams each year. No stipend, no living, travel, accommodation or insurance support, and no bond or service obligation beyond ambassador activity capped at typically eight hours per semester.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Eligibility is determined by domicile, not nationality. Applicants must be permanently domiciled in a country named for their regional round and must ordinarily and predominantly have resided there for the past three years; residence in the listed country solely for the purpose of full-time education does not establish domicile, so applicants educated abroad in that country are not eligible on that ground. programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to international fee-paying students domiciled in the countries named for each regional round. The North America undergraduate round covers Canada and the USA, and the South East Asia undergraduate round covers Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, so applicants from allowed regions are eligible in both verified rounds. The scheme page's wider country list, which includes Bangladesh, Botswana, Egypt, Ghana, India, Kenya, Mauritius, Nigeria, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, Vietnam and Zimbabwe, governs other regional rounds whose terms were not individually verified for this record.

Minimum grades are specified per accepted qualification rather than per subject, and the University may give greater credit to applicants for courses of study where students from their region are underrepresented.

supplements_or_initiatives: Humanitarian Scholarship: a separate University of Manchester undergraduate scheme listed on the same funding pages, for applicants whose circumstances meet the University's published Humanitarian Scholarship criteria; it is a distinct award and is not covered by this record.

GREAT Scholarships: the University participates in the GREAT Scholarship programme, including the GREAT Scholarship 2026 - University of Manchester (Bangladesh) which is already indexed in the live database. Those are separate British Council country-specific awards and are not covered by this record.

Science and Engineering International Excellence Awards: a Faculty of Science and Engineering scheme with 21 awards of GBP 5,000 per year for up to four years, automatic consideration, and a restriction to a specific country list. Its page states it is for students starting in 2025 and it is not listed among the 2027-entry undergraduate funding options, so it is a stale, separate scheme and no figure from it is used here.

Master's Global Futures awards: the same programme name covers more than 250 master's-level awards of GBP 12,000 as a one-off fee discount, with their own regional deadlines. They are a different degree level and are excluded from this record.

programme_detail_official.description: The Global Futures Scholarship is The University of Manchester's international merit scholarship for September 2027 entry, offering more than 350 awards across undergraduate and master's study with a total value of more than GBP 6 million. Undergraduate awardees receive GBP 12,000 per year for up to three years, applied as a discount on published overseas tuition fees and conditional on an overall average of at least 60% in exams each year. Eligibility is determined by domicile within regional country lists rather than by nationality, is limited to international fee-paying self-funded applicants entering directly into Year 1 of a full-time on-campus Manchester course, and excludes Medicine, Dentistry, Architecture and integrated foundation year courses. Application is separate from admission: candidates apply through UCAS and then complete a dedicated online scholarship form emailed to relevant applicants and offer-holders, submitting it by the regional closing date.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Part of the published overseas tuition fees only: GBP 12,000 per year for up to three years, applied as a fee discount and renewable subject to a 60% average in exams each year. Living costs, accommodation, travel, insurance and visa or immigration health surcharge costs are all outside the coverage, and no cash payment is made to the awardee.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are domiciled, not merely a national, in a listed country, and that you have predominantly lived there for the last three years; residence there solely for full-time education does not qualify.
Check the regional round that applies to you and read its own terms and conditions PDF, because the accepted qualifications, minimum grades, closing date and notification date differ by round.

Confirm your qualification is on your round's accepted list, then check both the course offer grade requirement and the scholarship minimum grade (for example A Level AAA, IB 36 with 666 at Higher Level, or three AP exams at 5,5,5).

Apply through UCAS as early as you can and no later than the Equal Consideration Deadline of 13 January 2027; if you apply after that date, you must hold an offer before you can be sent the scholarship form.
Monitor your email from December 2026 onwards for the dedicated scholarship application form link, and check spam folders.

Complete every section of the form. List pending qualifications and predicted grades on both the UCAS application and the scholarship form, because merit is assessed from them when final results are not available.
Submit the form by your regional closing date, 4 March 2027 (North America) or 23 April 2027 (South East Asia), and well before the end of the day since no closing time is published.
Make Manchester your Firm UCAS choice by 5 May 2027 (North America) or 7 June 2027 (South East Asia).
Check the English level and test validity on your course profile, and ensure the test will still be within two years of its date at the start of Welcome Week.
Budget the uncovered share: tuition beyond GBP 12,000 per year, accommodation, living costs, travel, insurance and visa or health surcharge costs.
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the award is open to all international students. It is restricted to applicants domiciled in specific listed countries, so applicants from other countries should not apply on the expectation of being considered.
Waiting for final results before applying. Predicted grades and previous examination results are used, and pending qualifications must be listed on both applications.
Submitting more than one scholarship application when applying for multiple courses. Only the first application is considered.
Leaving sections of the online form incomplete. Incomplete applications are not considered at all.
Submitting after the regional closing date. The University states late applications cannot be accepted under any circumstances, and there is no grace period.
Not keeping Manchester as the Firm UCAS choice by the regional date, which can cause the award to be retracted and reallocated.
Applying for Medicine (MBChB), Dentistry (BDS), Architecture or an integrated foundation year course, all of which are excluded.
Assuming the award covers living costs. It is a tuition-fee discount only, and no cash is paid to the awardee.
Being sponsored by an external government agency or commercial funder, which breaks the self-funded requirement.
Having previously studied at a higher education institution in the UK, which makes the applicant ineligible.
Relying on a secondary source that still calls the award the 'Global Excellence Scholarship' or quotes GBP 6,000 per year, neither of which appears on the official site for 2027 entry.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees beyond the GBP 12,000 annual discount. The award is a partial waiver, so the balance of published overseas tuition fees remains payable for every year of study.

Living costs, with no stipend or living allowance attached to the award. No monthly cost-of-living figure is recorded here because the University's cost-of-living or accommodation figures were not read on an official page for this record; read the University's international students pages before budgeting.
Accommodation, whether University halls or private rental, not covered by the award.
Travel to and from the United Kingdom, not covered in either direction.
Visa costs and the immigration health surcharge, not covered; awardees must still be able to demonstrate to UKVI that they can pay the remainder of tuition and living costs.
Health insurance, which is not covered by the award.
Study materials, books and equipment, not covered.
The English language test fee, not covered.
Any UCAS application fee, which sits outside the award and is not stated on the scholarship pages.
Lost earnings or opportunity cost, which no tuition discount addresses and should be treated as a real component of the total cost for applicants from outside the UK.
document_audit: The University publishes no document checklist for the scholarship itself; awards are made from the UCAS application, predicted or achieved grades and the online application form. This list is derived guidance, not an official requirement.
UCAS application for a full-time, on-campus undergraduate course starting September 2027, submitted through UCAS with institution code 3737.
Personal statement within the scholarship application form, the strength of which is explicitly assessed.
Predicted grades and results of previous tests and examinations, listed on both the UCAS application and the scholarship form where final results are pending.
Final results for pending qualifications, shared by the regional deadline (15 August 2027 for the South East Asia round).
Evidence of English proficiency meeting the course offer conditions, unless an exemption applies for a UKVI majority English-speaking country or for Canada.
Confirmation of Firm UCAS status showing Manchester as the firm choice, by the regional date.

alerts.message: The award is officially the Global Futures Scholarship for 2027 entry, worth GBP 12,000 per year for up to three years. No 'Global Excellence Scholarship' page exists on the official site and no GBP 6,000 per year figure is published, so ignore secondary sources using those figures.

Eligibility requires permanent domicile in a listed country and predominant residence there for the last three years. Holding the nationality is not enough on its own, and residence there solely for full-time education does not count.

The North America undergraduate round closes 4 March 2027 and the South East Asia round closes 23 April 2027. There is no single scheme-wide deadline, and no closing time is published, so use your own round's date and submit early.
The award is only retained while you average at least 60% in exams each year. For Year in Industry courses, continuation into Year Four depends on the Year Two result.
This is not full funding. The discount applies to tuition fees, no cash is paid to you, and living costs, accommodation, travel, insurance and visa costs must be met from other funds.

This is not automatic on admission. You must receive and complete the online scholarship form the University emails to relevant applicants and offer-holders, and only the first form you submit is considered.

Medicine (MBChB), Dentistry (BDS), Architecture and integrated foundation year courses are excluded, as are blended and distance-learning programmes. Applying unsuccessfully for an excluded course and being offered another course does not stop you applying.

The award cannot be combined with any other University of Manchester award. If your combined Manchester awards exceed total tuition fees, tuition is simply covered in full and no payment is made to you.

submission_workflow: Apply for the course through UCAS, ideally by the Equal Consideration Deadline of 13 January 2027, using institution code 3737.
If you applied after that date, secure an offer of a study place before the regional scholarship closing date, because only offer-holders can be sent the form.
Watch for the University's email containing the dedicated online scholarship application form, sent from December 2026 onwards.
Complete every section of the form, including pending qualifications and predicted grades, and submit once.
Confirm submission before the regional closing date, 4 March 2027 (North America) or 23 April 2027 (South East Asia).
Make Manchester your Firm UCAS choice by 5 May 2027 (North America) or 7 June 2027 (South East Asia).
Meet all academic, non-academic and English offer conditions by the regional date (15 July 2027 or 13 August 2027 for North America depending on qualification; 15 August 2027 for South East Asia).
On award, register on the course and ensure the tuition-fee discount is applied, then keep your average at 60% or above each year to retain it through Years 2 and 3.
If you need to change programme or interrupt study, get International Office approval in writing first, as the award depends on it.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The round-specific terms and conditions PDF used for this record is headed 'The University of Manchester Global Futures Scholarships - North America - Undergraduate Scholarships' and covers 'Global Futures Scholarships 2027', addressing Year 1 entry applicants, the UCAS Equal Consideration Deadline and firm-choice dates, and referencing the standard three-year undergraduate course structure and the Years One, Two and Four treatment for Year in Industry courses.
